newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU assures new members on environmental rules.
newsitem.headline: EU assures new members on environmental rules.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday there had been progress in work to ensure that the bloc's three newest recruits would not need to cut environmental standards by the end of a four-year transition period.
When Austria, Finland and Sweden joined the European Union in 1995, they were allowed to keep stricter national health and environmental rules until the end of 1998.

During these four years, the 15-nation EU would review its own standards in a bid to bridge the gap in terms of environmental rules. The EU executive has repeatedly sought to assure the new members that they would be able to keep their environmental legislation also after the transition period.
It is a sensitive issue in the three new EU countries, which take pride in being at the forefront when it cames to introducing tough rules to help clean up the environment.

"It is a clear aim and goal of the Commission to make sure that legislation or other arrangements are in place before the end of 1998 so that member states do not have to lower the standards in the field of environment," said Peter Jorgensen, the spokesman of EU Environmental Commission Ritt Bjerregaard.
"There are various ways of trying to achieve that goal but that is the goal of the Commission; they should not lower their standards."

In a statement, the EU executive said the "state of play, the good progress already achieved and further steps to be taken in the review process" had been discussed at a meeting in April with representives from the three newcomers.
For example, the problem concerning different classification and labelling requirements for dangerous substances had been solved for 13 and 11 substances in Austria and Sweden respectively.
Bjerregaard "underlines that the Commission principle of ensuring a high level of environmental protection in the Union will be fully applied to the review process," the Commission statement said.
